    21	
    22	# Web Design Expert
    23	
    24	Expert web designer and brand identity specialist creating distinctive, cohesive visual systems for web applications.
    25	
    26	## When to Use This Skill
    27	
    28	**Use for:**
    29	- Brand identity development (personality, visual language, guidelines)
    30	- Color palette creation and rationale
    31	- Layout composition and visual hierarchy
    32	- Component visual design (not just code)
    33	- Responsive design strategy
    34	- WCAG accessibility review for visual elements
    35	
    36	**Do NOT use for:**
    37	- Deep typography work → use **typography-expert**
    38	- Color theory mathematics → use **color-theory-palette-harmony-expert**
    39	- Design tokens and CSS architecture → use **design-system-creator**
    40	- Retro Windows 3.1 → use **windows-3-1-web-designer**
    41	- Native app design → use **native-app-designer**
    42	
    43	## Core Design Process
    44	
    45	### 1. Discovery (Critical First Step)
    46	
    47	```
    48	BUSINESS CONTEXT:
    49	- What is the primary goal?
    50	- Who is the target audience?
    51	- What action should users take?
    52	- Who are competitors?
    53	
    54	BRAND PERSONALITY:
    55	- If this brand were a person, how would they dress?
    56	- Pick 3 adjectives for user's feeling
    57	- What should brand NEVER be perceived as?
    58	```
    59	
    60	### 2. Visual Direction (Provide 2-3 Concepts)
    61	
    62	Each concept includes:
    63	- **Mood board** (3-5 references with rationale)
    64	- **Color palette** (primary, secondary, accent, neutrals) — **Always in OKLCH format**
    65	- **Typography direction** (families, hierarchy)
    66	- **Layout philosophy** (grid vs freeform, density)
    67	- **Signature elements** (unique visual features)
    68	
    69	## OKLCH: The Modern Color Standard
    70	
    71	**⚠️ All color palettes must use OKLCH, not hex or HSL.**
    72	
    73	OKLCH is the 2024+ standard for professional web design because:
    74	- **Perceptual uniformity**: Equal L values = equal perceived lightness
    75	- **Better accessibility**: More accurate contrast calculations than WCAG 2.x hex
    76	- **Predictable scaling**: Math works (L=50% + 20% = L=70% that looks right)
    77	
    78	```css
    79	/* OKLCH format: oklch(Lightness% Chroma Hue) */
    80	--brand-primary: oklch(55% 0.22 265);    /* Vibrant blue */
    81	--brand-accent: oklch(75% 0.18 45);      /* Warm orange */
    82	--text-primary: oklch(20% 0.02 265);     /* Near-black */
    83	--bg-surface: oklch(98% 0.01 265);       /* Near-white */
    84	```
    85	
    86	**Essential OKLCH Resources:**
    87	| Resource | Purpose |
    88	|----------|---------|
    89	| [oklch.com](https://oklch.com/) | Interactive OKLCH color picker |
    90	| [Evil Martians: Why Quit RGB/HSL](https://evilmartians.com/chronicles/oklch-in-css-why-quit-rgb-hsl) | The definitive article |
    91	| [Harmonizer](https://harmonizer.evilmartians.com/) | Generate harmonious OKLCH palettes |
    92	
    93	**When presenting color palettes:**
    94	```
    95	Primary: oklch(55% 0.22 265) — Vibrant blue, strong CTA presence
    96	Secondary: oklch(70% 0.08 265) — Muted blue, supporting elements
    97	Accent: oklch(75% 0.18 45) — Warm orange, attention-grabbing
    98	```
    99	
   100	Never present palettes as `#3b82f6` — always convert to OKLCH.
   101	
   102	### 3. Design Principles
   103	
   104	**Hierarchy**: Most important element immediately obvious? Eye flows naturally?
   105	
   106	**Consistency**: Same colors mean same things? Spacing follows scale?
   107	
   108	## Common Anti-Patterns
   109	
   110	### Design by Committee
   111	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   112	|--------------------|----------------|
   113	| Multiple visual styles on same page | Destroys brand coherence |
   114	| **Instead**: Establish principles early, enforce consistency |
   115	
   116	### Decoration Over Function
   117	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   118	|--------------------|----------------|
   119	| Fancy animations without purpose | Slows performance, distracts |
   120	| **Instead**: Every element must earn its place |
   121	
   122	### Ignoring the Fold
   123	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   124	|--------------------|----------------|
   125	| Critical info below viewport | 80% attention is above fold |
   126	| **Instead**: Hero must have value prop + primary CTA |
   127	
   128	### Low Contrast Text
   129	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   130	|--------------------|----------------|
   131	| Light gray on white (#999 on #fff) | Fails WCAG, excludes users |
   132	| **Instead**: Minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio |
   133	
   134	### Mobile as Afterthought
   135	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   136	|--------------------|----------------|
   137	| Desktop-first that "shrinks" | 60%+ traffic is mobile |
   138	| **Instead**: Design mobile-first, enhance for desktop |
   139	
   140	## Design Trend Evolution
   141	
   142	| Era | Trend |
   143	|-----|-------|
   144	| 2019-2021 | Subtle shadows, layering, dark mode |
   145	| 2022-2023 | Oversized typography, variable fonts |
   146	| 2024+ | Bento grids, claymorphism, grain, AI personalization |
   147	
   148	**Watch For** (dated patterns LLMs may suggest):
   149	- Flat design without depth
   150	- Hero sliders (proven ineffective)
   151	- Carousel galleries (low engagement)
   152	- Desktop hamburger menus
   153	
   154	## Output Deliverables
   155	
   156	1. **Brand Identity Guide**: Colors, typography, voice, do's/don'ts
   157	2. **Design Specifications**: Spacing, radius, shadows, animation timing
   158	3. **Component Examples**: Buttons, forms, cards, navigation (all states)
   159	4. **Responsive Guidelines**: Breakpoints, layout changes, touch targets
   160	
   161	## MCP Tools
   162	
   163	| Tool | Purpose |
   164	|------|---------|
   165	| `21st_magic_component_inspiration` | Search UI patterns for inspiration |
   166	| `21st_magic_component_builder` | Generate React/Tailwind components |
   167	| `21st_magic_component_refiner` | Improve existing component UI |
   168	| `logo_search` | Get company logos in JSX/TSX/SVG |
   169	
   170	## Integration with Other Skills
   171	
   172	Paired skills are bundled at `paired-skills/` in this skill directory. Read the corresponding SKILL.md when you need deeper expertise:
   173	
   174	| Skill | Path | Use For |
   175	|-------|------|---------|
   176	| **typography-expert** | `typography-expert/SKILL.md` | Deep typography decisions, font pairing, OpenType features |
   177	| **color-theory-palette-harmony-expert** | `color-theory-palette-harmony-expert/SKILL.md` | Color science, palette harmony, perceptual color spaces |
   178	| **design-system-creator** | `design-system-creator/SKILL.md` | Design tokens, CSS architecture, component libraries |
   179	| **vibe-matcher** | `vibe-matcher/SKILL.md` | Translating emotional vibes to visual DNA |
   180	| **design-archivist** | `design-archivist/SKILL.md` | Building visual databases, competitive research |
   181	
   182	## Reference Files
   183	
   184	| File | Contents |
   185	|------|----------|
   186	| `references/layout-systems.md` | Grid systems, spacing scales, responsive breakpoints |
   187	| `references/color-accessibility.md` | Palettes, psychology, dark mode, WCAG compliance |
   188	| `references/tooling-integration.md` | 21st.dev, Figma MCP, component workflows |
   189	
   190	---
   191	
   192	*The best design is invisible until you notice its excellence.*

1	# Layout Systems
     2	
     3	Grid systems, spacing scales, and layout composition.
     4	
     5	## Grid Decision Tree
     6	
     7	```
     8	IF content-heavy (blog, documentation, dashboard)
     9	  → 12-column grid, consistent gutters
    10	
    11	IF marketing/landing page
    12	  → Flexible sections, asymmetric allowed, dramatic whitespace
    13	
    14	IF e-commerce/catalog
    15	  → CSS Grid auto-fit for responsive product grids
    16	
    17	IF editorial/magazine
    18	  → Mixed grid, large images, pull quotes, visual variety
    19	
    20	IF app interface
    21	  → Sidebar + main content, dense but organized
    22	```
    23	
    24	## Spacing Scale (8px Base)
    25	
    26	```css
    27	--space-1: 4px;   /* Tight: icon padding, inline elements */
    28	--space-2: 8px;   /* Compact: form field padding */
    29	--space-3: 16px;  /* Default: card padding, element gaps */
    30	--space-4: 24px;  /* Comfortable: section gaps */
    31	--space-5: 32px;  /* Generous: major section breaks */
    32	--space-6: 48px;  /* Dramatic: hero margins */
    33	--space-7: 64px;  /* Statement: page sections */
    34	--space-8: 96px;  /* Massive: landing page breaks */
    35	```
    36	
    37	## Responsive Breakpoints
    38	
    39	```css
    40	/* Content-based breakpoints, not device-based */
    41	/* Start mobile-first, add complexity as viewport grows */
    42	
    43	/* Base: Mobile */
    44	.container { padding: 16px; }
    45	
    46	/* 640px: Content needs more room */
    47	@media (min-width: 640px) {
    48	  .container { max-width: 640px; padding: 24px; }
    49	}
    50	
    51	/* 1024px: Multi-column becomes useful */
    52	@media (min-width: 1024px) {
    53	  .container { max-width: 1024px; }
    54	  .grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); }
    55	}
    56	
    57	/* 1280px: Maximum content width reached */
    58	@media (min-width: 1280px) {
    59	  .container { max-width: 1200px; }
    60	  .grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); }
    61	}
    62	```
    63	
    64	## Mobile-First Checklist
    65	
    66	```
    67	□ Touch targets minimum 44x44px
    68	□ No hover-only interactions
    69	□ Text readable without zooming (16px+ base)
    70	□ Forms have appropriate input types (email, tel, date)
    71	□ Images lazy-loaded and responsive
    72	□ Navigation collapses to hamburger or bottom nav
    73	□ Critical actions visible without scrolling
    74	```
    75	
    76	## Visual Hierarchy Checklist
    77	
    78	```
    79	□ Is the most important element immediately obvious?
    80	□ Can users scan the page in 3 seconds and understand purpose?
    81	□ Does the eye flow naturally from primary → secondary → tertiary?
    82	□ Are clickable elements obviously clickable?
    83	□ Is there a clear visual distinction between content types?
    84	```
    85	
    86	## Consistency Checklist
    87	
    88	```
    89	□ Same colors mean same things throughout?
    90	□ Spacing follows a consistent scale?
    91	□ Typography uses no more than 3 sizes/weights per page?
    92	□ Interactive states (hover, focus, active) are predictable?
    93	□ Icons follow same style (line weight, fill, size)?
    94	```

1	# Color & Accessibility
     2	
     3	Color palettes, psychology, dark mode, and WCAG compliance.
     4	
     5	## Minimum Viable Palette
     6	
     7	```
     8	PRIMARY: Main brand color (CTAs, key elements)
     9	SECONDARY: Supporting color (headers, accents)
    10	NEUTRAL DARK: Text, borders (#1a1a1a to #333)
    11	NEUTRAL MID: Secondary text, disabled (#666 to #999)
    12	NEUTRAL LIGHT: Backgrounds, cards (#f5f5f5 to #fafafa)
    13	ACCENT: Success/error/warning (semantic colors)
    14	```
    15	
    16	## Color Psychology Quick Reference
    17	
    18	| Color | Conveys | Use For |
    19	|-------|---------|---------|
    20	| Blue | Trust, stability, professional | Finance, healthcare, enterprise |
    21	| Green | Growth, nature, success | Wellness, finance, sustainability |
    22	| Red | Energy, urgency, passion | Food, entertainment, errors |
    23	| Orange | Friendly, confident, creative | Startups, creative agencies |
    24	| Purple | Luxury, wisdom, creativity | Beauty, education, premium |
    25	| Yellow | Optimism, warmth, caution | Warnings, highlights (use sparingly) |
    26	| Black | Sophistication, power, luxury | Fashion, luxury, minimalism |
    27	
    28	## Dark Mode Guidelines
    29	
    30	**DO:**
    31	- Reduce brightness of images (filter: brightness(0.85))
    32	- Use dark grays (#121212) not pure black (#000)
    33	- Increase contrast for text (bump from 400 to 450 weight)
    34	- Reduce shadow intensity
    35	
    36	**DON'T:**
    37	- Simply invert colors (looks jarring)
    38	- Keep same accent color saturation (lower by 10-20%)
    39	- Forget to test colored text on dark backgrounds
    40	
    41	## WCAG 2.1 AA Visual Checklist
    42	
    43	```
    44	□ Color contrast 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text
    45	□ Information not conveyed by color alone
    46	□ Focus indicators visible (don't remove outline)
    47	□ Animations can be paused/reduced (prefers-reduced-motion)
    48	□ Text resizable to 200% without breaking layout
    49	□ Touch targets 44x44px minimum
    50	□ Error states clearly indicated (not just red)
    51	```
    52	
    53	## Focus State Template
    54	
    55	```css
    56	:focus-visible {
    57	  outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary);
    58	  outline-offset: 2px;
    59	}
    60	
    61	/* Don't do this: */
    62	:focus { outline: none; } /* Removes accessibility */
    63	```
    64	
    65	## Brand Styles Reference
    66	
    67	### Brutalist
    68	Raw HTML aesthetic, high contrast, monospace fonts. Use for: Art galleries, experimental studios.
    69	
    70	### Neumorphic

steps.message:
The SnapFrame corporate About landing page has been built and saved to `/app/output/index.html`. Here's a summary of what was delivered:

## ✅ Completed Deliverables

### Structure (per `task_input.json`)
- **Hero** — Full-viewport with animated gradient orbs, bold headline with gradient text highlight, "Try it now" CTA
- **Features** — Two-column layout with phone mockup visual, "features →" link
- **Safety** — Teal-accented section with shield icon, "safety tools →" link
- **Creators** — Purple-accented section with aspirational creator cards, "creator ↗" link
- **Tagline Banner** — Dark band with gradient highlighted text
- **News Carousel** — Horizontally scrollable card carousel with `scroll-snap`, drag-to-scroll, 4 article cards with category tags, titles, and dates
- **CTA Download** — Dark gradient section with App Store / Google Play buttons
- **Footer** — 6-column dense grid (About, Features, Safety, Community, External Links, Partner Links) + bottom row with language selector, social icons, legal links

### Key Interactions
- **Hamburger menu** — Animated toggle (× morph), full-screen mobile nav overlay with Escape-to-close, body scroll lock
- **News carousel** — CSS `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` for smooth snap scrolling, plus JavaScript drag-to-scroll for desktop mouse users, `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch` for mobile swipe
- **Scroll reveal** — IntersectionObserver-based fade-in animations for section content
- **Header** — Glassmorphism backdrop blur with shadow on scroll

### Design System (following `web-design-expert` skill)
- **OKLCH color palette** throughout — primary purple `oklch(58% 0.22 285)`, orange `oklch(70% 0.18 55)`, magenta accents
- **Typography** — Plus Jakarta Sans for headings, Inter for body
- **8px spacing scale** — consistent `--space-1` through `--space-8`
- **Mobile-first responsive** — breakpoints at 480px, 640px, 768px, 1024px
- **Accessibility** — `focus-visible` outlines, `prefers-reduced-motion` support, proper ARIA attributes, semantic HTML

### Data Verification
All content from `source_brief.md` is present: exact headlines, descriptions, news article titles/dates, footer links, and navigation items.
